messages:
Alex: Quick proposal — add a short-lived per-org routing exception flow in the console. Use-case: security/sales need a temporary direct route to dedicated infra for troubleshooting or contract commitments. Keep it auditable and gated. Thoughts?

Jordan: Interest. Agree on short-lived. Question on precedence: should these exceptions beat header-based pins (x-org-header) or be lower priority? My vote: exceptions should be highest priority but clearly visible in audit trails. :eyes:

Maria: From Sec: we need an identity binding (who created it), a mandatory reason field, and approver rules for >72h. Audit retention options: 90/365 days. Also require email/Slack notif to sec when any exception is created. No silent route failures — if the target pool is unavailable, fall back and create an incident ticket.

Toby: Implementation notes: store exception as a TTL key in routing-kv with expiry. Beware cache propagation delays — some edge agents may still route during a few-second window after expiry. Need an invalidation broadcast when exceptions are removed. Also watch KV cardinality (don't perma-leak entries).

Alex: UX idea: console modal with fields: org selector, duration (1h/4h/24h/72h/custom), reason (short text), approver (optional auto-lookup), toggles for `pin model-variant` and `bypass autoscale`. Show short cost estimate after selection. Keep flow optimistic but require justification for >24h.

Jordan: Matching semantics example to discuss precedence and eval order:
```
match {
  header "x-org-id" == "goldbank"
  override {
    route: "dedicated_pool:goldbank_v2"
    ttl: 4h
  }
}
```
This would be injected at highest priority in the route matcher. If a header pin also exists, exception wins.

Maria: +1 to that syntax. Add a `created_by` and `approved_by` fields in audit payload. Require conditional approver for durations >72h. Also add an automated review job that flags orgs with repeated exceptions in last 30d.

Toby: Telemetry plan: emit `org_exception.created` with labels org, actor, duration; `org_exception.expired`; `org_exception.failed_fallback` when target route unreachable. Dashboards: per-org counts, avg latency delta, per-exception cost delta. Alert if more than N active exceptions or sustained cost delta >X%.

deploy-bot: config change `org-exceptions/ui-ttl` deployed to staging at 1765432150 by CI.

Jordan: Proposed rollout: enable in staging, then canary with 5 orgs for 48h (monitor cost/latency + failed_fallback rate), then ramp to 20% of orgs. If telemetry shows increased failed_fallback or >2% cost delta, pause and revert. :thumbsup:
